title: required init & Self
hints: `Self(...)` constructs the dynamic type — which only works if every subclass has that init.
Mark the init `required`. `Dragon` re-declares it and doubles the level; `Goblin` inherits it.
`class func make(level: Int) -> Self { Self(level: level) }`.
jsBridge: `required init` forces every subclass to implement that initialiser, so `Self(level:)` can build the dynamic subclass type. JS gets this free with `new this.constructor(...)`. Swift needs the guarantee to type-check it.

compass.q: `new this.constructor()` works in JS because constructors are always callable. Why does Swift need `required` to allow `Self(...)`?
What happens if a subclass adds a stored property but forgets the `required init`?
